items.title: 52035_Eddie Durham oral history interview
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Well, now, this is when -- let's see, Dickie Rouse says that you and Basie got together on a whole lot of things now, though, for the band, because the band was the band's personnel was changing a bit, wasn't it?

ctx.x: good memory. Lunceford went to Europe and he had -- Lunceford had some 300 numbers in his repertoire. And I never pulled my book out, never. And when I go to Basie and play and go back up to Lunceford, I still didn't have to pull it out. Which might not have been so good for me then, because I remembered a lot of things myself. But, boy, they didn't pull no book out for me in those bands.

Well, now, this is when -- let's see, Dickie Rouse says that you and Basie got together on a whole lot of things now, though, for the band, because the band was the band's personnel was changing a bit, wasn't it?
Yeah, well, I gave it a story -- we didn't get on anything -- well, Digger Wells went in my place.
